I found out I had a grandson when he texted me asking why I never came to his games.
The number wasn’t saved in my phone. Just ten digits, area code 610, same as mine. The message came through at 11:42 on a Tuesday night.
“Hi. This is Ryan. Michael’s son. I play baseball at Riverside Park on Saturdays at 10. How come you never come?”
I read it once.
Then again.
Then I set the phone on the kitchen table and stared at it as if the words might rearrange themselves into something I understood.
Michael’s son.
Michael had a son.
Michael had a son named Ryan who played baseball at Riverside Park on Saturdays at ten, and I didn’t know any of it because I hadn’t spoken to Michael in twelve years. The last time I saw my son, he was twenty-eight years old. Thanksgiving 2014. He brought Julie home and told us they were getting married.
I’d met Julie twice. Once at a barbecue. Once at Easter dinner. She was polite. Quiet. Worked as a dental hygienist. She brought flowers for Ellen both times and helped clear the plates without being asked. None of that was the problem.
The problem, as I saw it then, was that Michael was two semesters away from finishing his engineering degree at Penn State. He…
